actions.name: exploited Log4Shell vulnerability in VMware Horizon server
actions.description: The threat actors exploited Log4Shell for initial access to the organization’s unpatched VMware Horizon server.

actions.name: ran PowerShell commands adding exclusion rule to Windows Defender
actions.description: The actors ran PowerShell commands that added an exclusion rule to Windows Defender allowing bypass of virus scans.

actions.name: downloaded and executed XMRig cryptocurrency mining software
actions.description: The exploit payload downloaded mdeploy.text from 182.54.217[.]2/mdepoy.txt to C:\users\public\mde.ps1, which when executed downloaded file.zip containing XMRig miner and associated files.

actions.name: created Scheduled Task RuntimeBrokerService.exe executing RuntimeBroker.exe daily as SYSTEM
actions.description: The exploit payload created a Scheduled Task named RuntimeBrokerService.exe that executed RuntimeBroker.exe daily as SYSTEM to maintain persistence.

actions.name: used RDP and DefaultAccount to move laterally to VMware VDI-KMS host
actions.description: After initial access, the actors used RDP and the built-in Windows user account DefaultAccount to move laterally to a VMware VDI-KMS host.

actions.name: downloaded PsExec, Mimikatz, and Ngrok tools
actions.description: The actors downloaded around 30 megabytes of files including PsExec, Mimikatz, and Ngrok from transfer.sh server associated with 144.76.136[.]153.

actions.name: executed Mimikatz to harvest credentials and created rogue domain administrator account
actions.description: The actors executed Mimikatz on VDI-KMS to harvest credentials and created a rogue domain administrator account.

actions.name: used rogue domain administrator account to propagate via RDP to multiple hosts
actions.description: Using the newly created rogue domain administrator account, the actors leveraged RDP to propagate to several hosts within the network.

actions.name: manually disabled Windows Defender via GUI and implanted Ngrok executables and configuration files on multiple hosts
actions.description: Upon logging into each host, the actors manually disabled Windows Defender via the GUI and implanted Ngrok executables and configuration files to maintain persistence.

actions.name: used Ngrok to proxy RDP sessions for command and control
actions.description: The actors used Ngrok to proxy RDP connections and to perform command and control, tunneling RDP over HTTPS connections to Ngrok domains.

actions.name: executed PowerShell command on Active Directory to obtain list of all machines attached to domain
actions.description: The threat actors executed a PowerShell command on the Active Directory to obtain a list of all machines attached to the domain.

actions.name: changed password for local administrator account on several hosts
actions.description: The threat actors changed the password for the local administrator account on several hosts as a backup in case the rogue domain administrator account was detected and terminated.

actions.name: attempted to dump LSASS process
actions.description: The threat actor was observed attempting to dump the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) process with task manager but was stopped by additional anti-virus.

relations.rationale: The PowerShell commands were run as part of the exploit payload following exploitation.
The exploit payload then downloaded and executed XMRig after running the PowerShell commands.
The Scheduled Task was created by the exploit payload after exploiting Log4Shell and gaining access.
After installing XMRig on the VMware Horizon server, the actors used RDP and DefaultAccount to move laterally.
Once established on the VDI-KMS host, the actors downloaded PsExec, Mimikatz, and Ngrok tools.
The actors then executed Mimikatz after downloading it on the VDI-KMS host.
Using the newly created rogue domain administrator account, the actors propagated via RDP to multiple hosts.
Upon logging into each host after propagation, the actors manually disabled Windows Defender and implanted Ngrok executables.
The actors used Ngrok to proxy RDP sessions for command and control after implanting Ngrok executables.
